summary: Deming Municipal Airport (DMN/KDMN) is a city-owned general aviation airport located about three miles southeast of downtown Deming, New Mexico, in the high desert of Luna County. The airfield has roots in the area's 20th-century military aviation history and now serves private, business, and emergency-service aircraft with two asphalt runways. It has no scheduled airline service, but it is a convenient stop near I-10 between El Paso and Tucson.
faqs:
Q: Does Deming Municipal Airport have commercial airline service?
A: No. DMN is a general aviation airport with no scheduled passenger airlines; the nearest major commercial service is El Paso International Airport (ELP), about two hours south.

Q: What runway and facilities does KDMN offer?
A: The field has two asphalt runways, 8/26 and 3/21, plus general aviation parking, hangars, and pilot services; check current fuel hours and NOTAMs before arrival.

Q: How far is the airport from downtown Deming?
A: It is roughly 3 miles southeast of downtown, typically a 5- to 10-minute drive by car.

Q: Is there U.S. Customs at DMN?
A: No. International general aviation flights should plan to clear customs at a designated port of entry such as El Paso before continuing to Deming.
transport_tips: The airport is a short drive from downtown Deming via East Pine Street/Country Club Road or NM-549, with I-10 access nearby. Rental cars and rideshare can be limited, so arrange a car or local shuttle in advance. For airline connections, most travelers drive to El Paso (ELP), about 2 hours south.
local_tip: Plan around afternoon density altitude and spring winds: early-morning departures from KDMN typically give the best climb performance and smoothest ride in this high-desert environment.
